enzyme_name: 6-phospho-beta-glucosidase (GH1 salicin-6-phosphate glucohydrolase)
organism_context: Bacteria with PTS beta-glucoside systems: E. coli AscB/BglB, Streptococcus pneumoniae BglA-2, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
rationale: GH1 6-phospho-beta-glucosidases are single-domain (beta/alpha)8 retaining glycosidases with one active site. Reported activity on both phosphorylated and unphosphorylated beta-glucosides is substrate promiscuity at that same site, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only direction a GH1 glycosidase runs in vivo; ModelSEED's '<' would require glucoside synthesis from glucose-6-phosphate plus saligenin, which is a glycosyltransferase reaction, not this enzyme.

enzyme_name: Catalase HPII (hydroperoxidase II) - self-catalysed conversion of its own protoheme IX to cis-heme d
organism_context: Escherichia coli; HPII is a clade-2 large monofunctional catalase
rationale: There is no separate 'heme D synthase': HPII catalase converts its own bound protoheme to cis-heme d as a peroxide-driven self-modification. HPII is explicitly a monofunctional catalase, in contrast to the bifunctional catalase-peroxidases (KatG) that carry both catalase and peroxidase activity.
direction_note: Oxidative heme b to heme d modification is irreversible, but the written '3 O2 -> 2 H+' has the wrong oxidant (H2O2 in vivo) and does not balance (H 30 vs 36, O 10 vs 6, charge -2 vs +4).

rationale: A model pseudo-reaction (abbreviation X00002) that collapses pimelate biosynthesis into one entry; no enzyme converts pyruvate plus oxaloacetate into pimelate. The real pimeloyl-thioester route to biotin runs through fatty-acid synthase with malonyl-ACP, BioC/BioH (or BioI), and NADPH.
direction_note: Mass-balancing forced O2 onto the product side, so the LLM's forward direction would evolve molecular oxygen while ModelSEED's reverse direction is oxidative pimelate breakdown; neither describes the biotin pathway the entry is named for.

enzyme_name: Butyryl-CoA beta-oxidation: acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (FadE) plus the multifunctional fatty acid oxidation protein FadB
organism_context: Escherichia coli FadB, the alpha subunit of the FadBA complex; eukaryotes use the analogous mitochondrial/peroxisomal trifunctional proteins
rationale: No single enzyme runs this three-step lump: the FAD-dependent step is FadE, a separate acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, while the hydratase and NAD-dependent dehydrogenase steps both sit on the single FadB polypeptide, which carries four catalytic activities on one chain.
direction_note: Beta-oxidation is the physiological direction; the free FAD/FADH2 pair in the equation also stands in for ETF-coupled electron transfer, which is what actually makes the dehydrogenase step irreversible.

enzyme_name: Complete palmitate beta-oxidation spiral: acyl-CoA synthetase (FadD), acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (FadE), multifunctional FadB, thiolase FadA
organism_context: Escherichia coli FadBA/FadD/FadE; the polyfunctional chain is FadB
rationale: Seven turns of the beta-oxidation spiral plus CoA activation are collapsed into one entry spanning at least four proteins, so no single enzyme catalyses it; of those, FadB is genuinely polyfunctional with four activities on one polypeptide (FadA thiolase is a separate subunit of the same complex).
direction_note: Forward is degradative beta-oxidation and is made effectively irreversible by the ATP-to-AMP+PPi activation step and subsequent pyrophosphate hydrolysis; ModelSEED's '<' would mean synthesising palmitate from acetyl-CoA via the degradative enzymes, which is not how fatty acid synthesis works.

enzyme_name: Complete octadecanoate beta-oxidation spiral: acyl-CoA synthetase (FadD), acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (FadE), multifunctional FadB, thiolase FadA
organism_context: Escherichia coli FadBA/FadD/FadE; the polyfunctional chain is FadB
rationale: Eight turns of the spiral plus CoA activation lumped into one entry, spanning four proteins, so no single enzyme catalyses it; FadB alone is polyfunctional, carrying hydratase, dehydrogenase, epimerase and isomerase activities on one chain.
direction_note: The ATP-to-AMP+PPi activation plus pyrophosphatase pull makes the degradative (forward) direction irreversible, so ModelSEED's reverse call is wrong regardless of the group-contribution numbers.

enzyme_name: Unidentified NAD(P)H-dependent reductase of 2-(sulfomethyl)thiazolidine-4-carboxylate (proposed coenzyme M biosynthesis step)
organism_context: Methanogenic archaea (Methanocaldococcus jannaschii, Methanosarcina); hypothetical step
rationale: The sulfoethylcysteine route to coenzyme M was a proposal and no protein was ever assigned to the thiazolidine-reduction step. White (2019) showed the methanogen enzyme ComF (MJ1681) converts sulfoacetaldehyde directly to 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate, bypassing sulfoethylcysteine entirely.
direction_note: If the step exists at all it is the reductive, biosynthetic direction toward sulfoethylcysteine (NADH consumed); the ModelSEED '<' has no enzymological support, but neither does the pathway, which is now superseded.

enzyme_name: Cytoplasmic cystine reductase activity - no single assigned protein (E. coli CydDC; thioredoxin/glutaredoxin systems; flavoprotein cystine reductase EC 1.8.1.6; mammalian TRP14/TXNDC17)
organism_context: Reaction entry is anonymous (rbs_386) with no EC; candidate systems span bacteria, fungi, plants and mammals
rationale: Several unrelated proteins reduce cytoplasmic cystine - the heterodimeric CydDC complex in E. coli, TRP14 in mammals, a flavoprotein cystine reductase in yeast/pea/Histoplasma - so the catalysing protein for this entry cannot be pinned down. CydDC would in any case be a two-subunit complex, which the protocol excludes from bifunctionality.
direction_note: The reductant (NAD(P)H, thioredoxin or glutathione) is absent - the equation supplies 2 H+ and no electrons - and it is that reductant pool, not the protein, that keeps cytoplasmic cystine reduced to cysteine.

enzyme_name: Choline/glycine-betaine ABC importer (substrate-binding protein + permease + ATPase; ChoXWV / OpuB / OpuC / ProU type)
organism_context: Rhizobium leguminosarum model entry (rll_92); characterised homologues in Sinorhizobium/Rhizobium (ChoXWV), Bacillus subtilis (OpuB/OpuC), Brucella abortus
rationale: An ABC importer is a multi-subunit complex (binding protein, membrane permease, nucleotide-binding ATPase), which under the protocol's exclusion is not a bifunctional enzyme; the one catalytic activity is ATP hydrolysis on the nucleotide-binding subunit.
direction_note: The extracellular substrate is written as chorismate (cpd00216) while the cytoplasmic product is choline (cpd00098), so the entry is not a transport of one species at all; ATP-driven import is nonetheless strictly unidirectional in the forward sense.

enzyme_name: Dihydrodipicolinate reductase / 4-hydroxy-tetrahydrodipicolinate reductase (DapB)
organism_context: E. coli, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Staphylococcus aureus, Sinorhizobium meliloti; homotetramer
rationale: DapB has a single NAD(P)H-dependent reductase activity; its two structural domains (dinucleotide-binding and substrate-binding) form one active site between them rather than carrying two activities.
direction_note: DapB's real product is 2,3,4,5-tetrahydrodipicolinate, not delta1-piperideine-6-carboxylate (a lysine-catabolism compound), and the equation loses a carboxyl carbon (C7 to C6); the NADPH-consuming reductive sense it is written in is nevertheless the correct one.

enzyme_name: Unidentified proton-coupled cysteine transporter
organism_context: Anonymous Rhizobium leguminosarum model entry (rll_530)
rationale: The entry carries no gene, EC or cross-reference, and bacterial cysteine movement is handled by several unrelated systems (exporters EamA/YdeD, Bcr, YfiK; cystine importers TcyP/TcyJLN; the CydDC complex), none of which is identified here.
direction_note: A H+-coupled secondary carrier is intrinsically bidirectional - direction is set by the proton-motive force and the cysteine gradient, not by the protein; note also that the extracellular species is ModelSEED's generic/D-cysteine alias (cpd00547, KEGG C00736) while the cytoplasmic one is L-cysteine.

enzyme_name: beta-glucuronidase (EC 3.2.1.31); KEGG assigns ortholog K01195, the GusA-type GH2 beta-glucuronidase
organism_context: KEGG rn00944 flavone/flavonol biosynthesis (plant flavone glucuronides, Scutellaria-type); the assigned ortholog is the bacterial GH2 enzyme
rationale: beta-Glucuronidases are single-active-site retaining glycosidases (GH2, or GH79 in plants); E. coli GusA is a homotetramer of identical one-activity chains and no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is effectively irreversible forward; ModelSEED's '<' would turn the glucuronidase into a glucuronosyltransferase, a different enzyme family that requires UDP-glucuronate rather than free glucuronate.

enzyme_name: 3-dehydroecdysone 3beta-reductase (3DE 3beta-reductase), an NADPH-dependent aldo-keto reductase; KEGG annotates the step as a 3beta-hydroxysterol dehydrogenase
organism_context: Insects - Spodoptera littoralis haemolymph enzyme, Bombyx mori; the ecdysteroid 'black box' of the Halloween pathway
rationale: The 3-oxo to 3beta-ol reduction in the ecdysteroid series is run by 3-dehydroecdysone 3beta-reductase, a single-activity member of the aldo-keto reductase superfamily; the epimeric 3alpha-reduction is done by a different protein (an SDR-family 3alpha-reductase), so the two activities are not fused.
direction_note: NADPH is replaced by '2 H+', leaving a 2-electron reduction with no electron donor (atoms balance but charge is off by 2); the reductive forward direction is the biosynthetic one toward 2,22,25-trideoxyecdysone.

enzyme_name: Presumed N-formylisoglutamine deformylase/amidohydrolase (unassigned)
organism_context: KEGG histidine metabolism (rn00340), isoglutamine branch; no organism or gene attached
rationale: KEGG R04879 carries no EC number, no orthology and no enzyme name, and PubMed has no record of a characterised formylisoglutamine deformylase; the isoglutamine branch of histidine degradation rests on old literature with no cloned protein.
direction_note: Formate, the obligatory second product of deformylation, is absent from both KEGG's and ModelSEED's equation (C6 to C5); read as a formamide hydrolysis, the forward direction is the irreversible one.

organism_context: KEGG vitamin B6 metabolism (rn00750); no organism attached
rationale: KEGG R05840 lumps 'glycolaldehyde + 2-oxobutanoate + alanine -> pyridoxine' with no EC and no orthology; it encodes precursor-incorporation results rather than a catalysed step, since the real routes are PdxA/PdxJ (DXP-dependent) or the Pdx1/Pdx2 glutamine amidotransferase complex (DXP-independent).
direction_note: Net flux in B6 metabolism is toward pyridoxine so the forward sense is right in spirit, but three substrates condensing with a carbon unaccounted for (C9 to C8) means no single enzyme's directionality is being described.

enzyme_name: CrtO, glycosyl-4,4'-diaponeurosporenoate acyltransferase
organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus crtOPQMN operon; staphyloxanthin biosynthesis
rationale: CrtO is a single-activity acyltransferase that esterifies the C6'' hydroxyl of the glucosyl moiety with 12-methyltetradecanoate as the final step of staphyloxanthin biosynthesis; the other four pathway activities sit on separate proteins (CrtM, CrtN, CrtP, CrtQ).
direction_note: MetaCyc writes the acyl donor as the free fatty acid, so the activated thioester (acyl-CoA/ACP) whose hydrolysis drives an EC 2.3.1.- acyl transfer is missing; that omission is exactly why the computed dG comes out at +46 to +49 kJ/mol and flips the direction against biosynthesis.

enzyme_name: 3'-N-debenzoyltaxol N-benzoyltransferase (DBTNBT), a BAHD-family acyl-CoA-dependent acyltransferase
organism_context: Taxus cuspidata / T. baccata; final acylation step of Taxol biosynthesis
rationale: DBTNBT is a single-activity BAHD N-acyltransferase that benzoylates the C13 side-chain amine; it is one of a set of separate, distinct Taxus acyltransferases (TAT, TBT, DBAT, BAPT), not a multidomain protein.
direction_note: Benzoyl-CoA and the released CoA are both missing, so the written reaction is a bare acylation with no energy source; the thioester is what makes the forward direction toward paclitaxel irreversible.

enzyme_name: Baccatin III: 3-amino-3-phenylpropanoyl-CoA transferase (BAPT), a BAHD-family acyltransferase
organism_context: Taxus cuspidata; C13 side-chain attachment step of Taxol biosynthesis
rationale: BAPT is a single-activity CoA-dependent acyltransferase that esterifies the C13 hydroxyl of baccatin III with the beta-phenylalanoyl group; the subsequent 2'-hydroxylation and N-benzoylation are catalysed by different proteins.
direction_note: beta-Phenylalanoyl-CoA and released CoA are absent from the equation, which is why the computed dG is +83 kJ/mol; with the real thioester donor the biosynthetic forward direction is the one that runs.

enzyme_name: Hepatic amidase / carboxylesterase acting as isoniazid amidohydrolase; KEGG assigns K01044 carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), EC 3.1.1.1 / 3.5.1.-
organism_context: Mammalian liver microsomes (human, rat, rabbit)
rationale: Direct hydrolysis of isoniazid to isonicotinic acid plus hydrazine is carried out by a liver amidase blocked by the carboxylesterase/amidase inhibitor BNPP. Esterase plus amidase activity in a carboxylesterase is one serine-hydrolase active site acting on two bond types, i.e. promiscuity rather than two fused catalytic domains.
direction_note: Amide hydrolysis is thermodynamically irreversible in the forward sense; no amidase resynthesises isoniazid from hydrazine and isonicotinate.

enzyme_name: beta-glucuronidase (GUS), gut bacterial GH2 enzyme (E. coli GusA and Lactobacillus/Bacteroides homologues); human lysosomal GUSB also acts
organism_context: Human gut microbiota - reactivation of SN-38 from SN-38G drives irinotecan-induced diarrhoea
rationale: GH2 beta-glucuronidases carry one retaining-glycosidase active site per chain (homotetramer in E. coli); no second catalytic activity is reported for any of the characterised gut-bacterial or human enzymes.
direction_note: Hydrolysis is the only direction; re-glucuronidation of SN-38 is a separate UGT1A1 reaction that requires UDP-glucuronate, not free glucuronate.

enzyme_name: None identified - non-enzymatic decomposition/hydrolysis of oxazaphosphorine metabolites
organism_context: Human cyclophosphamide metabolism (KEGG rn00982)
rationale: KEGG R08284 carries no EC, no orthology, and is flagged both 'unclear reaction' and 'incomplete reaction'; nornitrogen mustard arises by spontaneous hydrolysis of phosphoramide mustard, not by an enzyme acting on carboxyphosphamide, which is itself the ALDH-derived dead-end detoxification product.
direction_note: The equation also loses most of the molecule (C7 to C4) with no products named, but whatever the real chemistry it is an irreversible breakdown - carboxyphosphamide cannot be reassembled from nornitrogen mustard.

enzyme_name: NAD(P)H-dependent aldehyde/carbonyl reductase (aldo-keto reductase), by analogy with the aldophosphamide-to-alcophosphamide step
organism_context: Human/mammalian cytosol; ifosfamide metabolism (KEGG rn00982)
rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from chemistry, not confirmed: KEGG assigns no enzyme to R08290, but the matching cyclophosphamide step (aldophosphamide to alcophosphamide) is run by an NADPH-dependent cytosolic carbonyl/aldo-keto reductase, and aldo-keto reductases are single-activity monomeric enzymes.
direction_note: NAD(P)H is replaced by '2 H+' so the 2-electron reduction has no donor (KEGG itself flags the entry 'unclear' and 'incomplete'); the aldehyde-to-alcohol reduction direction is nevertheless the one that occurs physiologically.

enzyme_name: None - spontaneous beta-elimination of carbamic acid from 3-carbamoyl-2-phenylpropionaldehyde (CPPA)
organism_context: Human/rat felbamate bioactivation
rationale: In felbamate bioactivation CPPA loses its carbamate non-enzymatically to give atropaldehyde (2-phenylpropenal); the enzymatic steps in that pathway are the upstream esterase and alcohol dehydrogenase reactions, not this elimination.
direction_note: The carbamate leaving group is missing from the products (C10 to C9); the elimination is irreversible and runs only forward, after which atropaldehyde is trapped by glutathione via GSTs.

enzyme_name: Microsomal epoxide hydrolase (mEH, EPHX1)
organism_context: Human and mammalian liver endoplasmic reticulum; the main route clearing carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide
rationale: mEH is a single alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold catalytic domain with one Asp-His-Glu triad and one activity; its reported role as a sodium-dependent bile-acid transport protein is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional.
direction_note: Epoxide hydration is irreversible; mEH cannot re-cyclise the trans-10,11-diol back to the epoxide, so ModelSEED's '<' is not a reaction any epoxide hydrolase performs.

enzyme_name: CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4), confirmed as the main catalyst converting 2-hydroxycarbamazepine to 2-hydroxyiminostilbene
organism_context: Human liver microsomes; carbamazepine bioactivation
rationale: CYP3A4 has one monooxygenase active site - its enormous substrate range is promiscuity, not a second activity - and its electron donor, NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase, is a separate protein (unlike self-sufficient fused P450s such as P450 BM3, which genuinely are bifunctional).
direction_note: KEGG flags R08318 'incomplete reaction' and the equation drops the carbamoyl leaving group (C15 to C14) along with O2 and NADPH; the real route is a CYP3A4 oxidation to the iminoquinone followed by NADPH-mediated reduction, so the catabolic forward sense is correct but the entry collapses two steps.
